issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a Stock class and require the SealSaloon.stock attribute to be of type Stock (and static/final). However, the template provides an Inventory class that implements the expected stock behavior, and Stock.java in the template is empty. The solution also uses Inventory as the stock type. This mismatch in the expected class/type (Stock vs Inventory) is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students about which class to use and how to declare the shared stock attribute.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming and types consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement and UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock, or (B) rename Inventory to Stock (and remove or implement the empty Stock.java) so the template and solution match the specification. Ensure SealSaloon.stock is declared using the same class name in the task description and starter code (and is static/final as required).

issues.description: The template repository contains an empty Stock.java file while the working implementation for stock functionality is provided in Inventory.java. This redundant/empty file can mislead students into thinking they must implement Stock (creating duplicate functionality) or causes uncertainty about which class to extend or use.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the empty Stock.java from the template or fill it by delegating to/aliasing the Inventory implementation (e.g., implement Stock as a thin wrapper around Inventory or rename Inventory to Stock). Update the problem statement accordingly so there is a single, clearly named class students should use for stock management.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a Stock class (and a SealSaloon.stock attribute of type Stock), but the provided template and the solution use a class named Inventory to represent the same concept and provide the same methods (add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock). There is also an empty Stock.java file in the template. This inconsistent naming (Stock vs Inventory) can confuse students trying to map the problem requirements and UML to the code they must modify.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming consistent across artifacts. Either rename the Inventory class (and its file) in the template and solution to Stock, and update all references to use Stock, or update the problem statement and UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock. Also remove or populate the unused Stock.java file to avoid further confusion.
